claim: Misprints not in the authors’ errata, each confirmed by a reader on the page images of the corrected printing.
evidence_summary: p. 665 [1vi–viii] “[source: §4–5]” and the like, against [1v] “§§4–5”; p. 667 [3iib], an alternative question, “∗Did he return fortunately or surprisingly.”; p. 674 “In he wrote it by hand”, with the example in lower case; p. 679 [12ii] “Enterococcus faicium”; p. 686 “in(to)the room” and “on(to)the platform”, with no space after the bracket; p. 701 [31i] I left home before my parents divorced with no final stop; p. 701 “see Ch. 17, §10.2” with no final stop; p. 731 [26ii] “activities,]they” with no space after the bracket, and [26iv] with no final stop; p. 736 “a participial and verbless clause”, where or is meant; p. 737 “concessional adjuncts”, the book’s only use of concessional, where it elsewhere has concessive; p. 760 “a personal TV” for [70]’s “a personal TV set”; p. 774 “nervous break-down” for [3iv] breakdown.
finding: Candidates for the authors’ errata page. Faicium is inside quotation marks in the example and may reproduce its source, so a [sic] may be the better fix there.
proposed_wording: §§4–5; Did he return fortunately or surprisingly?; He wrote it by hand; faecium or [sic]; in(to) the, on(to) the; add full stops on p. 701 and to [26iv]; participial or verbless; concessive; personal TV set; breakdown

evidence.example: Readers’ page-image checks for each item.
evidence.locator: Section C, wording slips and punctuation.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
